title: Posterior Oblique Ligament

positions.as_written: Expect a knee with an injury here to feel unstable going into extension rather than in mid flexion, because that is when the structure should be tight.
Consider the meniscal attachment when an injury here is found.
Identify the gastrocnemius tubercle before the ligament in any posteromedial approach.
Treat it and the superficial collateral ligament as a reciprocal pair, in the way 2.8.2 and 2.8.3 treat the cruciate bundles.
Assess rotation at full extension when a medial injury is being staged.
Plan the femoral point from the gastrocnemius tubercle, and check it against the collateral ligament's point rather than measuring from the epicondyle alone.
Consider the posterior horn when advancing or reattaching the ligament, because the central arm carries it.
Protect the medial head of gastrocnemius origin when working at the femoral attachment.
Avoid treating a posteromedial repair as equivalent to a reconstruction of this ligament.
